The anonymous key 0000000000 runs at the lowest priority; register a free key at aihorde.net for higher priority. The provider uses a 120s timeout.

quirks.title: No tool calling
quirks.body: AI Horde's OpenAI-compatible proxy does not support function/tool calling. The provider drops tools, tool_choice and parallel_tool_calls so a tool-using request still completes as plain chat instead of failing.

quirks.title: Usage is kudos; tokens estimated
quirks.body: The proxy returns usage as {"kudos": N} with no token counts, and rejects max_tokens below 16 and a non-array stop. The AIHordeProvider normalizes the request (floors max_tokens, wraps stop) and synthesizes prompt/completion token estimates so analytics and savings math aren't zero.

quirks.title: Roster + context depend on online workers
quirks.body: Model availability changes as volunteer workers come and go, so a listed model can be temporarily unserved. The effective context window is set by the worker (often 4-8K), not the model's native maximum.

quirks.title: Uneven quality
quirks.body: Output quality varies by worker and quantization, and some workers append template or instruction text after the answer. Best treated as free fallback capacity, not a primary model.

quirks.title: Free volunteer queue, slow
quirks.body: AI Horde routes to volunteer-run workers through a priority queue, so latency is seconds to minutes, not the sub-second of hosted providers. The anonymous key 0000000000 runs at the lowest priority; register a free key at aihorde.net for higher priority. The provider uses a 120s timeout.

quirks.title: No tool calling
quirks.body: AI Horde's OpenAI-compatible proxy does not support function/tool calling. The provider drops tools, tool_choice and parallel_tool_calls so a tool-using request still completes as plain chat instead of failing.

quirks.title: Usage is kudos; tokens estimated
quirks.body: The proxy returns usage as {"kudos": N} with no token counts, and rejects max_tokens below 16 and a non-array stop. The AIHordeProvider normalizes the request (floors max_tokens, wraps stop) and synthesizes prompt/completion token estimates so analytics and savings math aren't zero.

quirks.title: Roster + context depend on online workers
quirks.body: Model availability changes as volunteer workers come and go, so a listed model can be temporarily unserved. The effective context window is set by the worker (often 4-8K), not the model's native maximum.

quirks.title: Uneven quality
quirks.body: Output quality varies by worker and quantization, and some workers append template or instruction text after the answer. Best treated as free fallback capacity, not a primary model.

quirks.title: Key is account_id:token
quirks.body: Cloudflare Workers AI authenticates with a combined credential in the form "account_id:token", not a bare token.

quirks.title: No API key required
quirks.body: Routes anonymously — the catalog ships a keyless sentinel row and calls work with no account or key.

quirks.title: Recurring free, 40 RPM, eval-only ToS
quirks.body: NVIDIA NIM replaced its depleting trial credits with a recurring per-account rate limit (40 RPM default, varies by model), verified June 2026. The trial ToS still scopes usage to evaluation/prototyping, not production.

quirks.title: Daily :free cap is account-wide
quirks.body: OpenRouter’s :free daily cap (50/day, or 1000/day once you have ever bought $10 of credits) is shared across ALL :free models on the account, not per model. Per-row rpd values here are therefore optimistic; the router’s cooldown handling absorbs the shared 429s.

quirks.title: Needs token room
quirks.body: Some free routes spend hidden reasoning tokens before visible output. Avoid tiny max_tokens values or requests can finish by length with empty content.

quirks.title: Thinking tokens use output cap
quirks.body: Gemini Flash can spend hidden thinking tokens inside maxOutputTokens. Avoid tiny max_tokens values or set thinkingBudget to 0 when provider support is available.

quirks.title: May emit reasoning prose
quirks.body: Cohere Command A Reasoning can spend output budget explaining its thought process on terse prompts. Use a larger max_tokens cap or a stricter no-reasoning instruction when exact short answers are required.

quirks.title: OpenRouter ultra route hangs
quirks.body: nemotron-3-ultra (550B) on OpenRouter takes 180s+ even on trivial prompts (heavily congested), so its OR row is seeded disabled. Use the OpenCode Zen route instead.

quirks.title: Anonymous tier is 2 req/min
quirks.body: OVH AI Endpoints anonymous mode is documented at 2 req/min per IP per model (observed even stricter across models). The 400 req/min authenticated tier requires a Public Cloud project with a payment method, so the catalog ships the keyless path. Treat as a breadth/fallback tier, not a throughput tier.

quirks.title: Zero-priced community routes can rotate
quirks.body: These are community routes: individual publishers (e.g. AkshayCoder48 "FreeAIXYZ", NamanSoni78, morriszdweck) register relays in Pollinations’ registry, and the catalog lists only the ones priced at zero Pollen. A publisher can re-price, rotate or withdraw a route, and Pollinations can delist it from the public registry, without notice; delisted routes may keep answering for a while. Use the 10 RPM per-user ceiling shown in the catalog and expect occasional fail-over.

quirks.title: Limited-time promo, roster rotates
quirks.body: OpenCode Zen free models are explicitly limited-time promotional access ("available for a limited time" per the docs), not a recurring quota. The roster rotates: qwen3.6-plus and minimax-m3 promos already ended. Expect any row here to die without notice; prompts/outputs may be used for model improvement.

quirks.title: Responses API only
quirks.body: OpenCode Zen exposes this model through POST /v1/responses rather than /v1/chat/completions. Clients and adapters must use the Responses API transport.

quirks.title: Zen serves the 550B fast
quirks.body: OpenCode Zen serves nemotron-3-ultra in ~2s with working tool calls where the OpenRouter route hangs — the live-verified path for this model.

quirks.title: Works with existing Zhipu key
quirks.body: glm-4.6v-flash is listed Free on Z.AI and answers 200 with the existing bigmodel.cn key; vision and structured tool calls both live-verified.

quirks.title: Free volunteer queue, slow
quirks.body: AI Horde routes to volunteer-run workers through a priority queue, so latency is seconds to minutes, not the sub-second of hosted providers. The anonymous key 0000000000 runs at the lowest priority; register a free key at aihorde.net for higher priority. The provider uses a 120s timeout.

quirks.title: No tool calling
quirks.body: AI Horde's OpenAI-compatible proxy does not support function/tool calling. The provider drops tools, tool_choice and parallel_tool_calls so a tool-using request still completes as plain chat instead of failing.

quirks.title: Usage is kudos; tokens estimated
quirks.body: The proxy returns usage as {"kudos": N} with no token counts, and rejects max_tokens below 16 and a non-array stop. The AIHordeProvider normalizes the request (floors max_tokens, wraps stop) and synthesizes prompt/completion token estimates so analytics and savings math aren't zero.

quirks.title: Roster + context depend on online workers
quirks.body: Model availability changes as volunteer workers come and go, so a listed model can be temporarily unserved. The effective context window is set by the worker (often 4-8K), not the model's native maximum.

quirks.title: Uneven quality
quirks.body: Output quality varies by worker and quantization, and some workers append template or instruction text after the answer. Best treated as free fallback capacity, not a primary model.

quirks.title: 123B has heavy queue (seeded disabled)
quirks.body: Behemoth-X-123B has deep queue depth (50s+ ETA even on trivial prompts). Seeded disabled; enable only if minute-scale latency is acceptable.

quirks.title: Auto route needs token room
quirks.body: Kilo auto/free can route to reasoning models that spend 100+ internal reasoning tokens. Avoid tiny max_tokens or a request can finish by length with empty content.

quirks.title: Safety classifier output
quirks.body: This route returns moderation/safety labels rather than normal assistant prose. Use it as a guardrail model, not a primary chat model.

quirks.title: Free route can change
quirks.body: Tencent Hy3 is currently free on these routes, but provider announcements describe some access as limited-time promotional availability. Monitor before aging into the monthly catalog.

quirks.title: Daily free quota
quirks.body: NaraRouter free access requires a no-card account key plus Telegram channel/link verification. The free plan is documented at 7M tokens/day and 10 req/min, with daily reset.

quirks.title: May emit thinking trace
quirks.body: OVH Qwen reasoning routes can include <think> blocks or reasoning prose. Strip or suppress the thinking trace when a plain answer is required.

quirks.title: Requires non-greedy sampling
quirks.body: Requesty rejected this route when temperature was 0 with greedy sampling. Use a nonzero temperature or provider-compatible sampling parameters.

quirks.title: Small $0.10/month routed credit
quirks.body: HuggingFace Inference Providers grants only ~$0.10/month of routed credit on the free tier (PRO is $2/month). Enough for light experimentation; exhausts quickly. Credits apply only to HF-routed requests.
